known_issues[+]: Snapshots of databases over two terabytes take hours rather than minutes, and while a snapshot is running the background compactor pauses, which means that write amplification climbs steadily for the whole duration of the job, so on a busy primary you should expect disk usage to grow by roughly the size of one full day of writes before it settles back down after the snapshot completes; the team says a fix is planned for a later point release but has not committed to a date, and in the meantime the documented workaround is to take snapshots from a replica instead of the primary, which only helps if you run a replica in the first place, and most small installs do not, because AcmeDB is still single-region and a second node in the same region mostly buys you a second copy of the same outage rather than any real protection against losing the region itself, which remains the larger risk.
